title: Scalar compatibility of point internal-Hom evaluation
statement:
Fix $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed $\Qlb$ [def-pod-conventions]. Write $R=\mathcal O_E$, $R'=\mathcal O_L$, $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$ and $B'=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,s}$. Let $P$ be a bounded complex of finite-projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and put $K=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline P$, $P^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,R)$ and $H=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{P^\vee}$. Assume $K,H$ are in $D^b_c(s,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and identify $H$ with $R\mathcal Hom_B(K,B)$ by the ordinary finite-projective Hom-complex model [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-pur-hom-complex]. Use the integral scalar-extension functor $T_{L/E}$ and the quotient-normalized operation comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]: after identifying $T_{L/E}$ with the strict quotient tower through the canonical completion map, its tensor component at every finite quotient is the canonical scalar-association map sending $(x\otimes\bar a)\otimes(y\otimes\bar b)$ to $(x\otimes y)\otimes\bar a\bar b$, compatibly with quotient transitions, and its internal-Hom arrow is the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation. Identify $T_{L/E}$ with ordinary derived extension $-\otimes_B^L B'$ by the canonical completion comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. The diagram comparing sections of the internal-Hom scalar arrow, through the specified sections comparisons [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], with the coefficient-module arrow
$$P^\vee\otimes_R R'\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{R'}^\bullet(P\otimes_R R',R')$$
commutes in the derived category. The lower arrow is the actual map $f\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes b\mapsto f(x)\otimes ab)$, with the two sides placed in the same signed Hom-complex convention. This commutative diagram is natural in maps of $P$, is the identity under the canonical identifications when $L=E$, and respects the specified associators for $E\subset L\subset M$. It remains commutative after rationalization to $E\subset L$, including naturality for localized morphisms.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-perfect-dual-scalar-calculus] to $R\to R'$ and $P$. It supplies the actual signed cochain map $\beta_P(f\otimes a)(x\otimes b)=f(x)ab$, its derived naturality, identity and tower equations, and its localization to $E\subset L$. Apply [lem-pod-completed-hom-scalar-transpose] to the given point models: the completed Hom arrow, conjugated by the specified $\chi$, is the sheaf realization $\gamma$ of this $\beta_P$. Its models and evaluation tensors have the completeness, constructibility and uniform finite-Tor hypotheses required there.

source.place: Second sentence: '$R\mathcal Hom$ at the point being computed over the coefficient ring'; finite-projective scalar/evaluation calculation.

proof.text: Use [lem-pod-completed-model-sections-transport] with $A=P^\vee$, $C=\operatorname{Hom}_{R'}^\bullet(P\otimes_R R',R')$, $v=\beta_P$ and $g=\gamma$. For the source and target unit maps write $q_E=e_A^{-1}$ and $q_L=e_C^{-1}$; these are precisely evaluation on $1\otimes x$ by [lem-pod-point-completed-evaluation] in the finite-projective Hom models. The transport equality gives $q_L\Gamma(s,\delta)\varphi_H^{-1}(q_E^{-1}\otimes1)=\beta_P$. Equivalently $q_L\Gamma(s,\delta)=\beta_P(q_E\otimes1)\varphi_H$, the claimed square with the specified vertical maps. On $f\otimes a$ evaluated at $x\otimes b$ it is $f(x)ab$; both uncurried evaluations have the same sign $(-1)^{\deg x\deg f}$ by [lem-pod-perfect-dual-scalar-calculus].

proof.text: The derived naturality and normalized identity/tower equations of [lem-pod-perfect-dual-scalar-calculus] and [lem-pod-completed-hom-scalar-transpose] pass through the exact sections transport of [lem-pod-completed-model-sections-transport], which uses the specified associators. The rationalized equation follows from that node by tensoring over $R'$ with $L$; [lem-pod-perfect-dual-scalar-calculus] identifies its module Hom models with those over $E$ and $L$. The comparisons are linear: scalar extension and precomposition are linear, as is the displayed formula for $\gamma$. For a localized morphism $u/\varpi_E^n$, the last clause of [lem-pod-completed-model-sections-transport] applies to these linear comparisons and sends precomposition by it to precomposition by $u$ divided by $\varpi_E^n$. It proves naturality independent of the fraction representative, and also transports the identity and tower equations.
